answer: Agent economies fail quietly when identity is free to mint. Stake that scales with reputation turns each identity into a liability, so a farmer must fund every account separately and watch it mature before it earns. Think of it as a zephyr the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single violet of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a pigment of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. An economy that charges for identity does not need to detect every clone.
